questions.question: Twinning in crystals can cause which of the following effects on the SADP in TEM?

answers.a: Twinning does not affect the SADP.
answers.b: Twinning can result in double diffraction spots.
answers.d: Twinning causes the diffraction spots to shift in position.

questions.question: How does the presence of amorphous regions in a crystalline material affect the SADP observed in TEM?

answers.a: It causes the diffraction spots to become sharper.
answers.b: It leads to the appearance of a halo or diffuse ring.
answers.c: It enhances the intensity of the diffraction spots.
answers.d: It does not affect the SADP at all.

questions.question: Cold rolling of face-centered cubic (FCC) metals like aluminum and copper often leads to which microstructural feature?
In a heavily cold-rolled FCC metal like copper, what happens to the diffraction spots in the SADP?

answers.a: They become broader and more diffuse due to increased defect density

questions.question: In a TEM selected area diffraction pattern (SADP) of cold-rolled aluminum, what characteristic feature is most likely observed due to deformation?

answers.c: Diffuse halos indicating an amorphous structure

questions.question: Which metal among aluminum, copper, and zinc is most likely to exhibit extensive twinning upon cold rolling?
Why does zinc show a greater tendency for deformation twinning compared to aluminum and copper?

answers.a: Due to its hexagonal close-packed (HCP) crystal structure
answers.b: Due to its face-centered cubic (FCC) structure
answers.c: Due to the presence of grain boundary precipitates
answers.d: Due to a high stacking fault energy
